The Centre has capped trade margins on 137 anti-cancer medicines at 30 percent, with the government estimating annual savings of Rs 2,500 crore for patients. But will the move actually make expensive cancer drugs more affordable?
The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) issued the order on 17 October, with revised prices set to take effect from 9 November. While the government expects maximum retail prices to fall by up to 70 percent, actual savings will depend on manufacturers' prices, competition among brands and hospital purchasing practices.
